title: HeterMV: Multi-view reasoning over source-aware heterogeneous evidence graph for multi-source fact verification
research_question: Can explicit source-aware heterogeneous graph modeling and multi-view evidence reasoning improve multi-source fact verification while suppressing irrelevant, redundant, or inconsistent auxiliary evidence?
methodology: HeterMV represents core evidence, surrounding context, and reference documents as distinct node types in a source-aware heterogeneous evidence graph and uses directed multi-relational propagation to aggregate auxiliary information toward core evidence. It constructs four reasoning views—multi-source fusion, core-corroboration, context-infusion, and knowledge-citation—and combines view-conditioned prompt tuning with cross-view consistency contrastive learning. The model is evaluated against state-of-the-art baselines on the public Check-COVID and FEVEROUS-S datasets using both gold-evidence and BM25-retrieval settings, with comparative evaluation, ablation studies, hyperparameter analysis, and case analysis described in the accessible preview.

key_findings.finding: The framework explicitly preserves source roles by representing core evidence, context, and reference documents as different node types and by using source-specific directed relations rather than homogenizing all evidence.

Four decoupled reasoning views are used to separate evidence perspectives, while view-conditioned prompt tuning aligns each perspective with the claim and cross-view contrastive learning is intended to reinforce supportive signals and suppress noisy ones.

On Check-COVID with 1,504 claims, HeterMV reports Micro-F1 improvements of 3.06 percentage points in the gold setting and 3.27 percentage points under BM25 retrieval over the compared state-of-the-art baselines.
On FEVEROUS-S with 29,890 claims, HeterMV reports Micro-F1 improvements of 1.72 percentage points in the gold setting and 1.41 percentage points in the corresponding BM25-retrieval setting.

The accessible article preview reports that ablation studies validate contributions from the framework's major components and that the evaluation also includes hyperparameter-sensitivity and case analyses.

limitations: The method is explicitly scoped to three forms of textual evidence—core evidence, local context, and reference documents—even though fact-verification evidence can also include tables, images, and knowledge graphs.
The reported evaluation is limited to two benchmark datasets, Check-COVID and FEVEROUS-S, so behavior outside those benchmark settings is not established by the accessible material.

Only an article preview and abstract-level material were accessible, so detailed per-class results, full ablation values, failure cases, and any author-stated limitations could not be independently inspected.
No public code repository was identifiable in the accessible article material.
raw_claims: HeterMV treats core evidence, context, and reference documents as semantically different evidence sources.
Directed multi-relational propagation aggregates auxiliary evidence into representations centered on core evidence.
The framework reasons through multi-source fusion, core-corroboration, context-infusion, and knowledge-citation views.
View-conditioned prompt tuning is used to align claims with evidence from different reasoning perspectives.
Cross-view consistency contrastive learning uses the core-corroboration representation as an anchor for supportive auxiliary signals.
The reported Check-COVID Micro-F1 gains are 3.06 percentage points with gold evidence and 3.27 percentage points with BM25 retrieval.
The reported FEVEROUS-S Micro-F1 gains are 1.72 percentage points with gold evidence and 1.41 percentage points in the corresponding retrieval setting.
The experimental section describes comparative evaluation, ablation studies, hyperparameter-sensitivity analysis, and a case study on two public datasets.
